species.notes: Compact southern highbush blueberry bred for mild-winter gardens (low chill, about 150 hours); stays leafy most of the year and suits a large pot or a raised bed. Needs acidic soil (pH 4.5 to 5.5) and steady moisture, so it is flagged wherever the soil is not acidic. Size, water, chill and fruiting months are general estimates.

species.notes: Southern highbush blueberry for mild winters (low chill, about 300 hours), upright and a little taller than Sunshine Blue; semi-evergreen. Plant it with a second variety nearby for a heavier crop. Needs acidic soil (pH 4.5 to 5.5) and steady moisture. Size, water, chill and fruiting months are general estimates.

fruit.source: General estimate for display; ripening months vary with variety, year and microclimate.

species.notes: Thornless, upright blackberry with a low chill need that suits mild-winter gardens; canes fruit in their second year, so cut the old ones to the ground after harvest. Best on a wire or trellis a foot or two from a path. Fruit is eaten by birds and people alike. Size, water, chill and fruiting months are general estimates.

species.notes: California native iris, forms clumps of dark evergreen blades; handles clay and part shade, and is toxic if eaten. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.
Evergreen California fern for shady spots; accepts clay loam if it drains. Wants some summer water. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.

Large evergreen fern for deep shade; clay is fine when it drains, and it needs regular water through a Los Angeles summer. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.

Evergreen, scented, sprawling currant for dry shade under trees; tolerates clay. Roots where stems touch the ground. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.
Evergreen shrub with spiny holly-like leaves, winter yellow flowers and blue berries; takes clay and dry shade. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.
Fine, arching evergreen sedge that fills dry shade and tolerates clay; a common lawn alternative. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.
Nearly indestructible in deep shade; accepts clay and neglect. Burns in strong sun. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.
Tough evergreen clumps with lavender flower spikes; tolerates clay, shade and heat. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.
Winter-blooming evergreen perennial for shade; likes alkaline clay. Toxic if eaten. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.
Strap-leaved plant with orange spring flowers for dry shade; protect from hard frost. Toxic if eaten. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.
Trailing, minty California native groundcover for moist shade; clay is fine. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.

Small, sweet berries from spring to fall; unlike garden strawberries it does well in part shade and does not send out runners. Grow it in amended soil or a raised bed where clay is heavy. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.

species.notes: Day-neutral strawberry that fruits from spring into fall in mild coastal climates, and bears through heat. Needs fast drainage and regular water: plant it in a raised bed or amended soil where clay is heavy. Size, water category, bloom months and soil needs are general estimates, unverified.

species.notes: Reliable white floribunda, light honey scent; prune hard in January. Thorns.
Butter-yellow, licorice scent, compact and shade-tolerant for a rose. Thorns.
Disease resistant, near-continuous bloom, tolerates heat and less water than hybrid teas. Thorns.
Classic dark red, strong fragrance; one stem per bloom, so cut flowers. Watch for powdery mildew. Thorns.
Cream flowers edged in red, very fragrant. Needs good drainage and deep water. Thorns.
Low, spreading mound of small pink flowers; holds up well in heat. Few thorns.
Old China rose; single flowers open buff, turn pink then crimson. Heat tolerant, near year-round bloom in LA, good for bees. Thorns.
Sweetheart-rose buds in big spring flushes, a few the rest of the year. Needs a trellis or fence and tying. Thorns.
Thornless, evergreen and very vigorous; one huge spring bloom. Needs a big structure and room; hard to keep small.
Native thicket-former with single pink flowers and red hips for birds. Suckers, so give it room. Thorns.
